description_good_justification: The README describes what onctl does (a CLI to manage virtual machines across cloud providers and local microVMs): <https://github.com/cdalar/onctl/blob/main/README.md>
interact_justification: The README covers installation, the issue tracker is used for feedback, and contribution instructions are in <https://github.com/cdalar/onctl/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md>.
contribution_requirements_justification: Requirements for acceptable contributions (coding standard, tests, license) are documented in <https://github.com/cdalar/onctl/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md>.
documentation_interface_justification: Command reference and usage are documented at <https://onctl.sh/docs/getting-started>, and every command provides `--help`.
sites_https_justification: The project site <https://onctl.sh>, the repository <https://github.com/cdalar/onctl> and release downloads are all served over HTTPS.
english_justification: Documentation, issues and pull requests are in English.
repo_interim_justification: All changes land on `main` through pull requests, so interim versions between releases are in the public git history.
version_unique_justification: Each release has a unique vX.Y.Z identifier: <https://github.com/cdalar/onctl/releases>
version_tags_justification: Each release is a git tag: <https://github.com/cdalar/onctl/tags>
release_notes_vulns_justification: No release so far has fixed a publicly known vulnerability with a CVE or similar identifier in onctl itself.
report_process_justification: Bugs are reported through GitHub issues, as described in <https://github.com/cdalar/onctl/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md>.
report_responses_justification: No bug reports were filed by outside users in the last 12 months; all issues filed in that period have been resolved and closed: <https://github.com/cdalar/onctl/issues?q=is%3Aissue>
enhancement_responses_justification: No enhancement requests were filed by outside users in the last 12 months; maintainer-filed requests in that period were implemented and closed.
report_archive_justification: GitHub issues are publicly readable and searchable: <https://github.com/cdalar/onctl/issues?q=is%3Aissue>
vulnerability_report_private_justificati: Private reports are accepted through GitHub private vulnerability reporting, as described in <https://github.com/cdalar/onctl/blob/main/SECURITY.md>.
vulnerability_report_response_justificat: No vulnerability reports were received in the last 6 months. SECURITY.md commits to an acknowledgement within 7 days.
build_floss_tools_justification: Built with the Go toolchain, make and GoReleaser, all FLOSS.
test_justification: An automated test suite using Go's standard `go test` framework is part of the repository; how to run it is documented in <https://github.com/cdalar/onctl/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md>.
test_invocation_justification: `make test` / `go test ./...`, the standard way for Go projects.
test_most_justification: Statement coverage is about 37% (Codecov). Much of the code is thin cloud-SDK glue that is validated by end-to-end runs against real providers rather than unit tests.
test_continuous_integration_justificatio: GitHub Actions builds and runs the test suite on every push and pull request: <https://github.com/cdalar/onctl/blob/main/.github/workflows/build.yml>
test_policy_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md requires tests for new functionality and bug fixes: <https://github.com/cdalar/onctl/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md>
tests_are_added_justification: Recent feature and fix pull requests include test changes alongside the code: <https://github.com/cdalar/onctl/commits/main>
tests_documented_added_justification: The test policy is part of the documented requirements for pull requests: <https://github.com/cdalar/onctl/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md>
warnings_justification: `go vet` and golangci-lint (staticcheck, govet, errcheck, ...) run on every push and pull request: <https://github.com/cdalar/onctl/blob/main/.github/workflows/lint.yml>
warnings_fixed_justification: The Lint job is a required status check on `main`, so warnings must be fixed before a change can merge.
warnings_strict_justification: golangci-lint and `gofmt -s`/`go vet`/`go mod tidy` checks are enforced as merge-blocking CI checks.
crypto_published_justification: onctl only uses SSH and TLS, both publicly published and reviewed protocols.
crypto_call_justification: onctl does not implement cryptography itself; it calls the Go standard library and golang.org/x/crypto.
crypto_floss_justification: All cryptography comes from the Go standard library and golang.org/x/crypto, which are FLOSS.
crypto_keylength_justification: Key exchange and ciphers are the defaults of golang.org/x/crypto/ssh and Go's crypto/tls, which meet NIST minimums. SSH keys are supplied by the user.
crypto_working_justification: Security mechanisms rely on Go's SSH and TLS defaults. MD5 appears only for non-security purposes: deriving short stable resource names, and the MD5 key fingerprint that the Hetzner API uses to look up an SSH key.
crypto_weaknesses_justification: Security mechanisms use the default algorithm sets of Go's SSH and TLS libraries. MD5 is only used for non-security purposes (resource naming and the key fingerprint format the Hetzner API requires).
crypto_pfs_justification: SSH (golang.org/x/crypto/ssh) and TLS 1.2/1.3 connections to cloud APIs use ephemeral (EC)DH key agreement.
crypto_password_storage_justification: onctl does not store passwords for authenticating external users.
crypto_random_justification: onctl does not generate cryptographic keys or nonces itself; those are produced inside Go's crypto libraries using crypto/rand. math/rand is only used for a non-secret VM name suffix.
delivery_mitm_justification: Releases are distributed over HTTPS (GitHub Releases, Homebrew tap, https://onctl.sh/get.sh), and release checksums are GPG-signed.
delivery_unsigned_justification: Checksums are published over HTTPS together with a GPG signature (checksums.txt.sig); nothing is retrieved over plain HTTP.
no_leaked_credentials_justification: GitHub secret scanning is enabled on the repository and reports no open alerts; CI credentials are stored as GitHub Actions secrets.
static_analysis_justification: CodeQL, golangci-lint (staticcheck, govet), govulncheck and Snyk run in CI: <https://github.com/cdalar/onctl/tree/main/.github/workflows>
static_analysis_common_vulnerabilities_j: CodeQL and Snyk Code look specifically for common vulnerabilities in Go code.
static_analysis_often_justification: Static analysis runs on every push and pull request.
dynamic_analysis_justification: A Go native fuzz test (FuzzAllocateFCIP) is in the repository and the test suite runs under the race detector (`go test -race`) in CI: <https://github.com/cdalar/onctl/blob/main/.github/workflows/build.yml>
dynamic_analysis_unsafe_justification: onctl is written in Go, a memory-safe language.
dynamic_analysis_enable_assertions_justi: CI runs the tests with the Go race detector enabled, and tests use testify assertions throughout.
dynamic_analysis_fixed_justification: Fuzzing and race-detector runs have not found any exploitable vulnerability; CI fails on any detected race.
